arguments.decision: How should the root package.json put Turborepo 2.11.5 into multi-package mode (needed for root tasks '//#name' next to the uv members' tasks) without the name collision between the npm package and the uv member both called wiki-consistency?
arguments.evidence: Measured 2026-09-29 in a copy of the trial worktree with Turborepo 2.11.5, experimentalPythonWorkspaces and a virtual root uv workspace: with "workspaces": ["packages/*"] in the root package.json (T001's choice), 'turbo ls' fails: 'Failed to add workspace "wiki-consistency" from packages/wiki-consistency/pyproject.toml, it already exists at packages/wiki-consistency/package.json', because packages/wiki-consistency has both a uv project and an npm project (it installs qmd with npm ci --prefix packages/wiki-consistency and its own package-lock.json). npm workspaces also make that npm project a member of the root npm install, alongside its separate package-lock.json. Without a workspaces field, or with "workspaces": [], Turborepo runs in single-package mode and rejects every '//#name' task ('Package tasks are not allowed in single-package repositories'). With a workspaces glob that matches no directory containing a package.json (tested: ["tools/none"]), 'turbo run check --dry=json' lists exactly the 26 intended tasks, including backfire#test, doc-regions#test and wiki-consistency#test. packages/wiki-consistency/package.json is an unchanged site (its classification is review), so renaming its npm package is outside the selected sites.

candidates.description: Set the root package.json workspaces to a glob that selects no npm package, so Turborepo runs in multi-package mode and the only packages are the uv members; document the reason next to it in the report.
Keep workspaces ["packages/*"] and rename the npm package in packages/wiki-consistency/package.json so the identities differ, making it a member of the root npm workspace.
Leave T001's workspaces glob and report that Turborepo cannot run this layout.

requirements: turbo run check lists every intended check task.
arguments.priorities:
User and repository priorities (verbose-broccoli, feature/turborepo, Linear CHE-32, a trial whose result is a report; nothing is merged):
1. The user chose to move the TypeScript side from Deno to Node.js and to run the three Python packages (backfire, doc-regions, wiki-consistency) as one native uv workspace under Turborepo's experimental Python support.
2. Change only the parts that must change; leave everything else as it is. The smallest change that reaches the goal wins.
3. AGENTS.md reuse order: first existing repository, runtime, standard-library or dependency functionality; then a stable upstream dependency; then an unstable upstream with the smallest patch; last, minimal glue. Minimize locally owned code; prefer reducing locally owned implementation over reducing dependency count. If the goal needs substantial new local implementation, stop and report instead.
4. Requirements that stay: built backfire plugins install offline, stay self-contained and write only into their own .venv; readiness proves the server runs from its own .venv.
5. Dropping a check, changing scope, changing governance documents, or changing the user's global tools (Node, npm, uv, Codex) is the user's decision, not the agent's.
